formation.title: The High Kingship of Ireland
formation.text:
The clans have united and the Lordship of Ireland is no more. For the first time in centuries, a single High King speaks for all of Erin. But the character of this new kingdom remains to be determined. The Brehon judges still remember the old laws, the filí still sing of ancient glories, and the people still live by the rhythms of the clan system. Yet the Atlantic stretches wide beyond our western shores, and the ports of Galway, Waterford, and Dublin hum with trade from across the sea.

Will we look inward to rebuild the Gaelic order that sustained our ancestors, or outward to the ocean that connects us to the world?

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

modifiers.name: Gaelic Resurgence
modifiers.text: The High King has restored the ancient laws and customs of the Gaelic order. Brehon judges settle disputes, the filí preserve the genealogies, and the clans rally to a sovereign Ireland free from foreign interference.

modifiers.name: Atlantic Kingdom
modifiers.text: Ireland's position at the edge of the Atlantic makes it a natural gateway between Europe and the wider world. The new kingdom builds ships, courts foreign merchants, and looks westward to the open ocean.

advances.name: Tower House Tradition
advances.text: Ireland's landscape is dotted with thousands of tower houses: fortified stone residences that served as both clan seats and defensive strongholds.

advances.name: Brehon Law
advances.text: The ancient legal code of Gaelic Ireland, administered by the breithemh judges, regulating land, marriage, honor, and social obligation.

event.title: The Revival of Brehon Law
event.text:
The Brehon legal tradition, which governed Irish society for over a thousand years, stands at a crossroads. These laws (composed by the breithemh judges and transmitted through generations of legal scholars) regulated everything from land tenure to marriage, from the price of honor to the treatment of the sick. Under English pressure, Brehon law retreated beyond the Pale, but it never died.

Now the question arises: should we formalize and strengthen these native courts, or gradually adopt the common law practices that dominate our neighbors and facilitate international commerce?

modifiers.name: Brehon Courts Restored
modifiers.text: The ancient Brehon courts have been restored to formal authority, settling disputes through native Irish legal tradition.

modifiers.name: Common Law Adoption
modifiers.text: English common law practices have been adopted alongside native tradition, facilitating international relations and standardizing governance.

advances.name: Cattle Lords
advances.text: Cattle are the foundation of Irish wealth. Lords measured their status in herds, and cattle raids were both economic and political acts.

advances.name: Tanistry
advances.text: The Gaelic system of elective succession, in which a tanist is chosen from among eligible kinsmen to succeed the chief.

advances.name: Bardic Schools
advances.text: The bardic schools of Ireland train the filí, poet-scholars who preserve genealogy, law, and history through rigorous oral and literary tradition.

advances.name: Tower House Defenses
advances.text: The tower houses of Ireland are improved with machicolations, murder holes, and thicker walls, creating a network of formidable strongpoints.

advances.name: Gaelic Confederation
advances.text: The great Gaelic lords form a confederation under the High King, balancing clan autonomy with collective defense.

advances.name: Monastic Schools
advances.text: Ireland's monastic tradition, which once earned it the title Island of Saints and Scholars, continues to nurture learning and literacy.

advances.name: Redshank Tradition
advances.text: Scottish mercenaries known as redshanks have long supplemented Irish armies. Their fierce reputation and cross-sea mobility make them valued allies.

advances.name: Atlantic Fisheries
advances.text: Ireland's western coast offers rich fishing grounds that sustain coastal communities and train a hardy population of seafarers.

advances.name: Manuscript Tradition
advances.text:
The tradition of illuminated manuscripts and scholarly copying, born in monasteries like Kells and Clonmacnoise, continues in Ireland's bardic schools.

Available in: Bardic School

advances.name: Gaelic Lordship
advances.text: The consolidation of Gaelic lordships under royal authority reduces internal conflict and strengthens the kingdom against external threats.

advances.name: Atlantic Raiders
advances.text: Irish privateers prey on enemy commerce along the Atlantic shipping lanes, turning Ireland's coastal position into a strategic advantage.

advances.name: Nine Years' War Reforms
advances.text: The military innovations of Hugh O'Neill (training kern in pike and musket, adopting European tactics) transform Irish warfare.

event.title: The Nine Years' War
event.text:
The great Gaelic lords Hugh O'Neill, Earl of Tyrone, and Red Hugh O'Donnell have waged a bitter struggle against English encroachment. At the Battle of the Yellow Ford in 1598, O'Neill's forces destroyed an English army, proving that Irish troops could match their opponents in open battle through discipline, use of firearms, and tactical innovation. O'Neill trained his kern in the use of pike and musket, creating the first modern Irish army.

Though the historical campaign ended in defeat at Kinsale, the military lessons endure. Irish warfare will never be the same.

options.text: The lessons of the Yellow Ford endure

advances.name: Irish Wool Trade
advances.text:
Ireland's sheep produce excellent wool, and the export trade grows steadily as English and continental merchants seek Irish fleeces.

Available in: Wool Cottage

advances.name: Hedge Schools
advances.text: When formal education is suppressed, the Irish establish clandestine outdoor schools where scholars teach Latin, Irish, mathematics, and catechism.

advances.name: Wild Geese
advances.text: Irish soldiers serving in continental armies form elite regiments renowned for their courage. The Irish Brigade becomes a legend across European battlefields.

event.title: The Flight of the Wild Geese
event.text:
Following the upheavals of war, thousands of Irish soldiers have departed for the continent, entering service in the armies of France, Spain, Austria, and beyond. These 'Wild Geese' carry Irish martial traditions to every corner of Europe. The Irish Brigade in French service will earn renown at Fontenoy, while the Ultonia and Hibernia regiments serve Spain from Flanders to the Americas.

This diaspora represents both a loss and an opportunity. The soldiers who return bring continental military expertise, while those who remain abroad forge connections that benefit Irish trade and diplomacy.

modifiers.name: Continental Veterans
modifiers.text: Soldiers returning from continental service bring the military discipline and tactical knowledge of Europe's finest armies.

modifiers.name: Diaspora Bonds
modifiers.text: The Irish abroad maintain close ties with their homeland, channeling trade connections and diplomatic influence back to Ireland.

advances.name: Linen Industry
advances.text: Linen production transforms the Irish economy. Flax cultivation and bleaching expand rapidly, making Irish linen famous across Europe.

advances.name: Provision Trade
advances.text:
Ireland's exports of salted beef, butter, and pork supply the Atlantic world, from the navies of Europe to the plantations of the Caribbean.

Available in: Linen Bleach Green

advances.name: Penal Resistance
advances.text: Despite restrictive laws, Irish institutions endure through underground networks of clergy, scholars, and community leaders.

advances.name: Whiskey Distilling
advances.text: Irish whiskey, distilled from barley and aged in oak, becomes one of Ireland's most celebrated exports and a symbol of national identity.

advances.name: Parliamentary Tradition
advances.text: The Irish Parliament, inspired by Grattan and the Volunteers, asserts legislative independence and the right to self-governance.

advances.name: Diaspora Networks
advances.text: The Irish diaspora spans the Atlantic world, creating networks of trade, influence, and solidarity that connect Ireland to every major port.

advances.name: Revolutionary Spirit
advances.text: The tradition of Wolfe Tone and the United Irishmen inspires a generation willing to fight for liberty, equality, and national sovereignty.

destiny.name: The Irish Destiny
destiny.text: Ireland stands unified under a single High King. The destiny of Erin (whether it shall rebuild the Gaelic world or forge an Atlantic empire) awaits.

event.title: The Irish Destiny
event.text:
The High Kingship is restored and Ireland speaks with one voice for the first time in centuries. The clans that once fought each other now look outward, united under a sovereign who commands the loyalty of all Erin.

The question is not whether Ireland shall be great, but what form that greatness will take. The Gaelic world extends beyond these shores: to the Hebrides, to Man, to the highlands of Scotland where our kinsmen still speak our tongue. Or perhaps our destiny lies not in the lands of our ancestors but upon the Atlantic itself, where Irish ships can carry Irish goods to every port in the known world.

destiny.name: Ri na nGael
destiny.text: Seize the Isle of Man and the Inner Hebrides to unite all Gaelic peoples under the High King. The Gaelic world stretches beyond Ireland's shores.

event.title: King of the Gaels
event.text:
The Isle of Man and the Inner Hebrides have fallen under the High King's authority. For the first time since the Norse invasions, the Gaelic-speaking world of the Irish Sea is united under a single ruler. The fishermen of Man, the warriors of Islay, and the clans of Ireland all acknowledge one sovereign.

This is the first step toward a greater vision: the reunification of all Gaelic peoples, from the bogs of Kerry to the highlands of Scotland, under one crown.

options.text: The Irish Sea is a Gaelic lake.

destiny.name: Gaelic Reconquest
destiny.text: The Gaelic heartlands of Scotland are reclaimed. Argyll and Edinburgh are taken, with Inverness, the gate of the Highlands, and Scone, where the kings of Scots were made on the stone that legend says came out of Ireland. A Gaelic kingdom spans both islands.

event.title: The Gaelic Reconquest
event.text:
Edinburgh has fallen. The Gaelic High King now rules from Dublin to the Lothians, commanding a realm that encompasses the ancient Gaelic heartlands of both Ireland and Scotland. The clans of Argyll, the islanders of the Hebrides, and the Highland chieftains have rallied to a banner that promises the restoration of Gaelic civilization across both islands.

But this reconquest can take different forms. A military alliance with the Highland clans would create an unbreakable martial tradition, channeling the fierce independence of the Gaelic warrior into a disciplined fighting force. Alternatively, the union of Irish and Scottish learning could spark a Gaelic cultural renaissance, reviving the scholarly traditions that once made the Gaelic world the light of Western Christendom.

modifiers.name: Highland Alliance
modifiers.text: The Gaelic clans of Ireland and Scotland are bound by military alliance, their combined raiding tradition empowering siege warfare and plunder, though the cost of maintaining such alliances strains the treasury.

modifiers.name: Gaelic Renaissance
modifiers.text: The union of Irish and Scottish learning sparks a revival of Gaelic scholarship, spreading institutions and prosperity while accelerating the construction of a new civilization.

destiny.name: Imperium Scottorum
destiny.text: Conquer London, York and Caernarfon and unite these islands under Gaelic rule. Hold Armagh, where Brian Boru was written into the Book of Armagh as Emperor of the Irish, and build the see of Patrick up to twice what it was. Become the supreme power of the British Isles with an empire worthy of Brian Boru's legacy.

conditions.text: Armagh is owned directly and has at least 20 development

event.title: The Empire of the Gaels
event.text:
London itself is in Irish hands. The High King of Ireland now commands the greatest empire these islands have ever known: not built by Norman lords or Saxon kings, but by the Gaelic peoples who were here before them all. From the bogs of Connacht to the banks of the Thames, the writ of the Ard Ri runs unchallenged.

This is a moment of supreme triumph, but also of choice. The sword that won this empire can keep it: channeling the spirit of Brian Boru into a warrior dynasty that holds its conquests through martial supremacy. Or the High King can look to Ireland's older tradition, the monastic learning that once earned it the title Island of Saints and Scholars, building an empire of the mind that outlasts any empire of the sword.

options.text: Let the sword of Brian Boru defend us.

modifiers.name: Sword of Brian Boru
modifiers.text: The martial tradition of Brian Boru lives on. Irish armies move swiftly and assault fortifications with terrifying ferocity, though such aggressive warfare leaves little time for the niceties of court prestige.

options.text: We shall be saints and scholars once more.

modifiers.name: Island of Saints and Scholars
modifiers.text: Ireland's monastic and scholarly traditions are reborn on an imperial scale, nurturing population growth and reducing the cost of construction, though the peaceful character of the court means higher military upkeep.

destiny.name: Merchant Princes of Galway
destiny.text: Establish Ireland as an Atlantic trading power. Build up gold reserves, develop the wool trade, and make Galway the equal of any European port.

conditions.text: A market the country is in

children.text: Wool is produced in the market
Wool is traded in the market

event.title: The Merchant Princes of Galway
event.text:
The Fourteen Tribes of Galway (the great merchant families who have dominated the city's trade for generations) now operate under the patronage of the High King. Galway's harbor, facing the open Atlantic, has become the commercial heart of Ireland. Wool, hides, and fish flow outward; wine, spices, and luxury goods flow in from Iberia, France, and the Mediterranean.

With royal backing and stable governance, the merchant princes are building something unprecedented: an Irish commercial network that can compete with the great trading cities of Europe.

destiny.name: The Western Passage
destiny.text: Reach across the Atlantic to the Azores and beyond. Build a dock at Galway to fit out the ships needed for oceanic trade.

conditions.text: Galway is owned and has a Dock or one of the port buildings that replace it (Dry Dock, Shipyard, Grand Shipyard, Naval Base)

event.title: The Western Passage
event.text:
Irish ships have reached the Azores, planting the green banner on Atlantic islands that serve as stepping stones to the wider world. Banking institutions have been embraced, giving Ireland the financial sophistication to fund oceanic ventures. The Atlantic, once a barrier, is becoming an Irish highway.

This is a pivotal moment. The navigators who charted these routes can be honored as a new tradition: training the next generation of Irish seafarers to explore further and fight harder on the open ocean. Alternatively, the commercial possibilities of the Azores route can be developed through factor houses: permanent Irish trading posts that gather intelligence, cultivate contacts, and channel goods back to Ireland.

modifiers.name: Navigator Tradition
modifiers.text: Irish seafarers are trained in the traditions of Atlantic navigation, exploring further and fighting harder on the open ocean, though the maritime focus draws men away from land service.

modifiers.name: Factor Houses
modifiers.text: Permanent Irish trading posts abroad expand diplomatic reach and gather intelligence, though families grown rich abroad heed the court less.

destiny.name: The Emerald Dominion
destiny.text: Build a transatlantic commercial empire. Hold Bermuda, accumulate vast wealth, and build Galway, the town of the fourteen merchant families, up to twice what it was.

conditions.text: Galway is owned directly and has at least 35 development

event.title: The Emerald Dominion
event.text:
From Galway to Bermuda, from the Azores to the fishing banks of the Atlantic, Ireland has built a commercial empire that spans an ocean. Irish merchants trade in every major port, Irish ships carry goods across thousands of miles of open water, and Irish gold fills the coffers of a kingdom that was once dismissed as a backwater.

The Emerald Dominion can take one of two final forms. A provision fleet (the organized export of Irish beef, butter, and agricultural surplus) can supply the navies and colonies of the Atlantic world, making Ireland the indispensable victualler of maritime civilization. Or Ireland can declare its ports open to all comers, creating free ports that attract merchants from every nation, making the island a neutral hub of global trade.

options.text: We shall feed the Atlantic world.

modifiers.name: Provision Fleet
modifiers.text: Ireland's agricultural bounty feeds the navies and colonies of the Atlantic world. Raw materials flow freely and naval costs are reduced, though the kingdom's dependence on peaceful commerce makes war a costlier proposition.

options.text: Declare our ports open to all nations.

modifiers.name: Free Port of Ireland
modifiers.text: Irish ports are declared open to all nations, improving foreign relations and binding subjects closer to the crown, though the open character of the kingdom means armies suffer greater attrition abroad.

units.name: Redshanks
units.text: Scottish-Irish mercenary infantry known for their distinctive untanned deer-leather leggings. Fast, aggressive fighters experienced in the rough terrain of the Highlands and Irish bogs.

units.name: Irish Pike
units.text: Disciplined formation infantry trained in the manner of Hugh O'Neill's reformed army. Combining traditional Irish ferocity with continental pike-and-shot tactics.

units.name: Wild Geese
units.text: Irish soldiers who served in continental European armies and returned with the discipline and tactical sophistication of professional warfare. Their experience in French, Spanish, and Austrian service makes them formidable veterans.

units.name: Irish Privateer
units.text: A fast, nimble raiding vessel built for Atlantic commerce warfare. Irish privateers exploit the island's position astride major shipping lanes to prey on enemy trade.

buildings.name: Tower House
buildings.text: A fortified stone tower, typically four or more stories tall, serving as a clan chief's residence and strongpoint. Ireland built more of these than anywhere else in the British Isles.

buildings.name: Bardic School
buildings.text: A school for the filí, the hereditary poet-scholars of Gaelic Ireland, where students spend years mastering the intricacies of verse, genealogy, and law.

buildings.name: Wool Cottage
buildings.text: A rural cottage where Irish families spin, comb, and process wool into cloth. The cottage industry sustains many farming households.

buildings.name: Linen Bleach Green
buildings.text: An open-air facility where woven linen cloth is spread on grass and bleached by sun and water, producing the famously white Irish linen.

buildings.name: Whiskey Distillery
buildings.text: A pot-still distillery producing uisce beatha, the water of life. Copper pot stills transform malted barley into smooth Irish whiskey.

buildings.name: High Cross Monastery
buildings.text: A great monastic complex centered on an ornate stone high cross, serving as a beacon of Gaelic learning, faith, and cultural authority in the tradition of Clonmacnoise and Glendalough.

buildings.name: Atlantic Exchange
buildings.text: A purpose-built commercial exchange where Irish, Iberian, and Atlantic merchants conduct the business of transatlantic trade, rivaling any bourse in Europe.

list.name: Brehon Law
list.text: The customary legal system of Gaelic Ireland, named for the breithem (judge), administered by hereditary learned families such as the MacEgans and O'Davorens. The code was civil rather than criminal, settling disputes through honour-price (eneclann) and compensation (eric) rather than state punishment. Its toleration of native arbitration was outlawed in stages, from the Statute of Kilkenny (1366) to the King's Bench ruling in the Case of Tanistry (1607).

list.name: Tanistry
list.text: The Gaelic system of elective succession in which the tanaiste, named during the king's lifetime, was chosen from the derbfine: the four-generation patrilineal kin group sharing a common great-grandfather. By privileging proven capability over primogeniture, tanistry produced effective war-leaders but also chronic succession crises. The English King's Bench struck it down in the 1607 Case of Tanistry.

list.name: Bardic Schools
list.text: Hereditary schools of the filidh, the learned class of Gaelic Ireland, sustained by aristocratic patronage between roughly 1250 and 1650. Pupils studied for up to twelve years to master the strict syllabic metres of Dan Direach, the genealogies of the great houses, and the lore of Brehon law. The schools collapsed with their patrons when the Plantations and the wars of the seventeenth century destroyed the Gaelic order.

list.name: Coyne and Livery
list.text: Coinmheadh is buannacht: the Gaelic exaction by which a lord billeted his kern, gallowglass, and bonnacht companies on the rural population, taking food, lodging, and forage without pay. The system maintained a standing military force at no cost to the lord's treasury, but the soldiers themselves enforced the levy on the peasantry, often ruinously. Repeatedly outlawed by Anglo-Irish parliaments and as repeatedly ignored by the lords.

list.name: Pale Administration
list.text: The Lord Deputy's chancery, exchequer, and Dublin Castle apparatus governing the four counties of the English Pale (Louth, Meath, Dublin, and Kildare). From 1471 the office was held almost continuously by the Earls of Kildare, who ran Ireland through a Gaelic-style network of alliances on behalf of the Crown. The Irish Parliament was summoned only when the Lord Deputy needed new laws or new taxes.

list.name: Surrender and Regrant
list.text: The Tudor policy, devised under Thomas Cromwell and pursued from the 1540s, by which Gaelic and Gaelicised lords surrendered their lands and customary titles to the Crown and received them back by royal charter under English primogeniture. The 1585 Composition of Connacht extended the system westward, replacing the multiple Gaelic tributes with a single land-tax and converting trícha céts into baronies. It dismantled tanistry and Brehon tenure with a stroke of the pen.
